subject: Post-demo: coordinating customer-led load window and streaming concurrency checks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Han <sara.han@stratuslabs.com>, Kevin Lopez <kevin.lopez@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: coordinating customer-led load window and streaming concurrency checks

Hi Sara / Kevin —

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate you walking through the estimated throughput for your realtime summarization feature. To keep momentum, here’s a concise recap and what we need from the Stratus team so we can schedule a customer-led load window (k6 + Locust hybrid) next week.

Quick recap of targets we discussed:
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300 ms for non-streaming endpoints; p99 < 800 ms target for streaming tails
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s for batched text-gen endpoints, burst to 600 req/s for short windows
- Peak concurrency: up to 500 concurrent model sessions overall, streaming concurrency up to 60 simultaneous streams
- Avg tokens/response: ~350 tokens; streaming average token emit rate ~15 TPS

What we need from you to run the customer-led test:
1) Confirm a 3-hour test window (please propose two options and timezone)
2) Shared k6/Locust scripts (you mentioned v2 today) and the traffic matrix CSV
3) Test account info: API key placeholder, target model id/version, and the tenant/environment URL
4) IP addresses/CIDRs to allowlist on our side and any NATs we should expect from your load generators
5) Ramp plan: steady-state vs sawtooth patterns, and whether you want a canary 10% run first

I can provision a test API key and a pre-warmed canary slot once you share scripts and preferred windows. Ben (cc’d) will provide the allowlist ranges and a lightweight runbook for the canary.

Next steps (proposed):
- You propose two windows by EOD Wed (Mar 30)
- Share scripts + traffic matrix by Thu so we can pre-check for auth/headers and token sizes
- Canary run Mon (Apr 5) if windows line up (we can move earlier if needed)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min sync if you want to walk through the script headers.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Han <sara.han@stratuslabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Lopez <kevin.lopez@stratuslabs.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: coordinating customer-led load window and streaming concurrency checks

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned on the targets. We’ll run our primary load from our east-coast k6 cluster (managed by our infra team) and a smaller Locust fleet for websocket streaming probes.

Proposed windows (all ET):
- Option A: Wed Apr 7, 10:00–13:00 ET
- Option B: Thu Apr 8, 02:00–05:00 ET (lower production traffic)

We’ll share the k6 script (stratus_test_script_v2.k6.js) and traffic_matrix_Q1.csv by Thursday morning. We do want a 15-min canary at 10% load at the start of the window. If canary looks good we’ll ramp to full.

Notes / questions for Redwood before the canary:
- Please provide an SSL endpoint and a temporary API key for the test tenant
- Can you confirm IP allowlist ranges we should add to our firewall?
- For streaming probes, do you recommend any connection keep-alive or heartbeat settings to avoid premature disconnects?

Attaching the k6 script and traffic matrix (stubs attached).

—Sara
Sara Han
Head of Platform Engineering
Stratus Labs

Attachments: stratus_test_script_v2.k6.js (javascript), traffic_matrix_Q1.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sara Han <sara.han@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: coordinating customer-led load window and streaming concurrency checks

Sara / Vanessa —

I provisioned a test tenant and stubbed a temporary API key for Stratus: TEST-STR-9x3 (we’ll rotate after the session). Endpoint: https://test-us.redwood.ai/stratus-tenant

Allowlist ranges (please add these to your outbound rules):
- 34.201.12.0/24
- 34.201.13.0/24
- 52.24.178.128/25

Notes for streaming probes and canary:
- Heartbeat: keepalive 30s, reconnect backoff 1s -> 16s
- We recommend a 60s KV cache warmup phase for scripted sessions that reuse prefixes — include warmup iterations in your traffic matrix
- For high concurrency streaming we suggest token-batched emission (group into 50-token chunks) to reduce syscall overhead on the runtime

I’ve uploaded a short runbook checklist (redwood-runbook-canary-checklist.pdf) to the shared drive and linked it here: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/customer-led-loadtests#stratus.

If you want, Soojin can join the canary window to monitor tail latencies in real time.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Lopez <kevin.lopez@stratuslabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Han <sara.han@stratuslabs.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: coordinating customer-led load window and streaming concurrency checks

Thanks Ben — good to have the ranges. We ran a quick internal canary this morning against the test endpoint at ~15% load (using the attached script). Results:
- Non-streaming endpoints: p95 ≈ 280 ms, p99 ≈ 670 ms — within target
- Streaming tails: we observed increased jitter when streaming concurrency exceeded ~40 streams; p99 spikes to ~1.6s on the worst runs
- Observed a 20% CPU spike on our clients when grouping tokens aggressively (we’re going to tune the emitter)

We’re going to tweak the emitter and add a 60s warmup iteration as suggested. Also curious whether Redwood can enable a lightly-quantized model variant for the stress window to reduce tail latency (we will accept minor quality variance for this test).

Soojin — could you advise on possible runtime flags or batching knob changes we can test during the canary?

Attaching current run output: traffic_matrix_Q1_results.json (small).

—Kevin

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Han <sara.han@stratuslabs.com>, Kevin Lopez <kevin.lopez@stratuslabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: coordinating customer-led load window and streaming concurrency checks

Thanks Kevin — great data and thanks for the quick canary. Next steps from Redwood side before the full window:

Action items:
- Soojin: provide two runtime flag sets to test (batching / kv-cache / quantization): will send by Thu 12:00 PT
- Ben: will enable a lightly-quantized model variant in the test tenant and document any expected quality deltas (done by Thu EOD)
- Stratus: finalize window choice (A or B) and deliver final scripts with warmup iterations by Thu 15:00 ET

Proposed full window: Wed Apr 7, 10:00–13:00 ET with a 15-min canary at 10:00. If you prefer the overnight window we can pivot — just confirm.

I’m adding the HubSpot deal record and shared runbook links here: https://hubspot.redwood.ai/deal/STR-2027-0412 and https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/customer-led-loadtests.

We’ll plan a 30-min post-mortem the same day to capture changes to the config and any follow-up engineering work.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
